one_liner: BigCommerce has broad REST+GraphQL APIs with OAuth app flow and static API-account tokens, free sandbox/trial stores, and an official storefront MCP server (plus a closed-beta store-management MCP).
auth_notes: App-level API accounts use OAuth where each app generates a token per installing store. Store-level and account-level API accounts provide static access tokens created in the control panel. Registering apps requires a Developer Portal account.
access_notes: A free sandbox store or trial store is available, and API credentials are generated under Settings > API Accounts. Publishing to the marketplace requires partnership, but draft apps do not.
blocker_notes: Per-store setup is needed (each customer creates an API account or installs the app), but this is not a real blocker. Marketplace publishing needs partnership.

evidence.quote: BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.
Store-level API accounts](/developer/docs/overview/api-fundamentals/api-accounts#store-level-api-accounts) include a static access token that does not change.
Sign up for a free BigCommerce trial store to test API calls and build integrations without affecting live data.
The developer sandbox is free of charge.
API accounts are used to authenticate requests to our APIs.
For everything else, use the [REST and GraphQL APIs](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference).
The BigCommerce MCP server lets AI agents interact with a BigCommerce storefront using purpose-built commerce tools.
Connections use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Your MCP client registers itself automatically, so there's no client ID or client secret to create or manage.
